title: On Windows a read-only Codex delegation runs with sandbox danger-full-access: nothing enforces read-only, and a probe child wrote files
outcome: A read-only Codex delegation on Windows cannot change files or run writing commands: either Codex's own read-only sandbox is used again because it now works on Windows (shown by a live probe), or the host puts every command of a read-only Codex child through a gate it controls, as it does for Claude and Kimi. Until then TermAl states the gap where the read-only policy is described, and the review freeze check remains what detects a reviewer's change.
acceptance: A live probe like the one on this item, run by a read-only Codex delegation on Windows against the landed build, is refused before it writes; the probe's exact commands and the refusal are recorded in a note.

A test pins the configuration the fix relies on for a read-only Codex child on Windows (the sandbox mode it gets, or the approval policy and the host gate's decisions for a writing command and a reading one).
The full five-stage gate passes on the exact reviewed tree, its run directory and diff hash cited in a note.
docs/features/agent-delegation-sessions.md says how read-only is enforced for Codex on Windows after the fix, and what it did before.

completion.summary: Read-only Codex delegations on Windows run in Codex's read-only sandbox again. They use a second shared Codex app-server (profile ReadOnlySandbox, its own CODEX_HOME scope, PATH without PowerShell 7, so the shell is Windows PowerShell 5.1), and each session's profile is pinned with its thread. Landed in 27bf0b6, live since the 23:31Z restart. The live probe was refused a write (23:32Z). The host credited the full gate test-b41e1a44 on the landed tree. The third independent evaluation, bb097f9c…, passed all four criteria. Follow-ups: w-27f08e988f1e (read-only children's Engram MCP calls refused), w-53ab42df726c (two-profile tests), w-5632f86d61c9, w-92c391ba7a73.
